subject: Clearsail renewal — exhibit consolidation & MSA clarifications
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@clearsail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@clearsail.com>, procurement@clearsail.com
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal & uplift — MSA items to resolve

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. We have internal sign-off on the commercial terms (18-month renewal, 25% capacity uplift, new burst pool) but procurement flagged three items in the MSA and the order form we need clarified before we can route to legal:

1) Exhibit references — Cleansail legal wants the coverage schedule pulled into the MSA rather than an external exhibit. They cited auditability.
2) Data retention / logs — asked for a 24 month retention baseline and a limit on aggregated telemetry exports.
3) SLAs — asks for explicit latency commitment for dedicated capacity during peak hours.

Attached is our procurement checklist and the preferred exhibit language. Can you route to your legal and ops team? We need final paperwork in the next two weeks.

Best,
Elena
Procurement Lead | Clearsail

Attachment: Clearsail_Procurement_Checklist.pdf (pdf)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@clearsail.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@clearsail.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal & uplift — MSA items to resolve

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list and the timeline. 

Quick notes:
- We can accommodate the coverage schedule being embedded into the MSA, but that will trigger a short legal review and may change the exhibit numbering.
- On retention: our standard hosted offering keeps detailed request logs for 12 months; we can offer 24 months on Dedicated under a limited export policy (aggregated telemetry only). Need legal to confirm exact Wording.
- SLA: Dedicated capacity has a 99.9% uptime SLA; specifying a latency commitment during peak windows is a contract-level ask. Ops/infra will need to validate the percentile and sequence-length assumptions.

Irene — looping you in to propose redline language and a path for embedding the coverage schedule. Mateo / Markus, can you prepare an updated order form that shows the 25% uplift and the new burst pool with an indicative cost delta?

I'll follow up once we have a draft redline.

Thanks,
Hannah
Director, Renewals | Redwood Inference

Signature: Hannah Schmitt, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@clearsail.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Nov 2027 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Renewal & uplift — MSA items to resolve

All — I reviewed Elena's notes. I put together an initial redline and a short summary of tradeoffs. Key points in the attached draft:

- Coverage schedule insertion: propose Section 3.2 (Coverage Schedule) with a versioning clause referencing the attached schedule and a single-source-of-truth clause (so changes require mutual written approval). This addresses Cleansail's auditability ask while limiting our ability to do unilateral updates.
- Data retention: offer 24 months for request/usage logs for Dedicated customers but limit exports to aggregated telemetry and auditing reports; add a clause requiring customer-signed data export request with 30-day lead time.
- SLA latency: recommend an operational appendix that defines latency targets by model class for peak windows (e.g., p50/p95 for short-form generation). This keeps engineering-nuanced detail out of the main MSA but provides contractual clarity.

I attached: Clearsail_MSA_Redline_v1.docx and an MSA_RollingSummary.pdf that summarizes the change impact for Sales/Ops. Please review and flag any business risks.

—Irene
Legal Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Clearsail_MSA_Redline_v1.docx (docx)
Attachment: MSA_RollingSummary.pdf (pdf)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@clearsail.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Order form update & cost impact

Team / Elena — attached is the updated order form spreadsheet that surfaces the 25% capacity uplift, the burst pool configuration, and the estimated monthly delta. I included a column that shows cost with and without the 24-month retention add-on.

High level:
- Base renewal (18 months): unchanged pricing.
- Capacity uplift (25%) increases committed monthly spend by ~18%.
- Burst pool (config: 50k peak tokens/day) is priced as an overage credit bucket; if Clearsail prefers a guaranteed burst, we should convert it to a reserved burst SKU (higher commit).
- Retention add-on: one-time configuration fee + marginal monthly storage fee (~$1.8k/month).

I recommend we present two options to the customer: (A) include retention and embed schedule in MSA; (B) standard 12-month retention + separate addendum for retention exports. Option A shortens procurement cycles at the cost of making the MSA slightly less flexible.

Attachment: OrderForm_CapacitySchedule_Clearsail.xlsx (xlsx)

-Mateo
From: Elena Park <elena.park@clearsail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@clearsail.com>, procurement@clearsail.com, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal & uplift — MSA items to resolve

Thanks, Hannah / Irene / Mateo — this looks promising. A couple quick clarifying asks from our side before legal will approve:

1) Can Redwood confirm the exact percentile for the latency target you propose (p95?) and whether it covers both standard and burst pools?
2) On the 24-month retention, Clearsail's security team needs assurance that exports will be limited and audited — would the customer-signed export request + 30 days be acceptable for us?
3) If we go with Option A (embed schedule in MSA), will changes to the schedule require a new signed amendment or is an email confirmation sufficient?

We prefer the faster path (Option A) if the export controls and latency percentiles are contractually clear. Also, can you provide a clean PDF of the redline (not the Word tracked changes) so internal stakeholders can circulate?

Best,
Elena
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@clearsail.com>, procurement@clearsail.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Renewal & uplift — MSA items to resolve

Elena — quick answers and next steps: 

1) Latency: Ops confirmed p95 for dedicated capacity (both base and burst pools) with the operational appendix defining model classes and a sequence-length profile. We'll include clarified language in the appendix and an engineering attestation statement.
2) Exports: the customer-signed export request + 30 days is acceptable; we'll add an audit trail and notify procurement when exports are processed.
3) Change process: embedding the schedule in the MSA requires a signed amendment for material changes; administrative numbering/formatting updates can be handled via mutual email confirmation. We'll add that distinction to the redline.

Action items: Irene will produce a clean PDF redline and a short cover note for Clearsail's legal. Mateo will attach the updated order form with the cost options. I'll schedule a 30-minute wrap-up call for Thursday to close outstanding items and agree on DocuSign path.

Thanks all — aiming to have the packet ready for Clearsail legal review by Wednesday COB.

-Hannah

Signature: Hannah Schmitt | Director, Renewals | Redwood Inference
